findings.body: The required command proof checks only activity.status at line 302 and event keys/count here. It never asserts the running action or that a review result appears in top-level events. Removing activity.action and filtering review results out of board.py's public event projection would leave the named proofs green. The RUNS tests inspect producer records, and test_machine_views.py:137–144 checks occurrences, which does not protect this separate events contract. Extend the existing real-command cases to assert the run's action and a close-produced review-result event, including its time, item and plain line, in both views.

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. Both machine views read events.jsonl without the writer guard at src/forge/board.py:203–204. On Windows, an overlapping reader can make this replacement raise PermissionError, failing the worker, reader, reviewer or test command while recording progress. Add bounded replacement retries, as codex._record already does at src/forge/codex.py:550–558.
findings.title: Handle Windows readers holding the progress file open

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. A structured missing-session result becomes error_during_execution followed by its diagnostic. The worker's prefix check at src/forge/worker.py:441–443 consequently misses it; the reader checks stderr at src/forge/story.py:732 although this decoder returns the diagnostic through stdout. Both paths refuse instead of starting a fresh session. Recognize the missing-session diagnostic in both callers while preserving other failures. The structured response is documented in the [upstream reproduction](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/40609).
findings.title: Preserve missing-session recovery for structured Claude errors
